title: Isle of Quel'Danas
body: The Isle of Quel'Danas rises from the sea north of Eversong Woods, and on its plateau lies the Sunwell, the fount of power that Dath'Remar Sunstrider's people kindled with water carried from the Well of Eternity. In the Third War Arthas marched the Scourge across the isle and used the Sunwell to raise Kel'Thuzad, and the defiled well was lost to the elves. In time the island was overrun by forces sworn to Prince Kael'thas, his Dawnblade and Sunblade with demons, naga and the Wretched at their side, all in the service of the Burning Legion. Against them the Aldor and the Scryers of Shattrath set aside their feud and landed as the Shattered Sun Offensive, setting out from their staging area to win back Sun's Reach piece by piece. The Offensive fights on for the town, while demons and Scourge clash along the Dead Scar and naga hold the Greengill Coast.

parts.body: On the plateau to the south, Kael'thas's servants and their demon allies have set to work to reignite the Sunwell, and they mean its power for the Burning Legion. Every gain the Offensive makes in Sun's Reach brings it a step closer to the plateau and the fight to stop them.
sources: creature_text 25162 groups 4, 16-17 (plateau to the south; reigniting the Sunwell with his demon friends)
quest 11481 description (developments at the Sunwell Plateau)

parts.body: In the end the Legion's designs on the Sunwell failed. Kil'jaeden, master of the Burning Legion, was turned back, and the Sunwell has been cleansed and burns pure once more. Ranger-General Halduron Brightwing's wardens now guard the plateau, admitting no one without his leave. The rest of the island is far from quiet: the Offensive's war against the Dawnblade, the demons and the naga goes on.

title: Shattered Sun Staging Area
body: The Shattered Sun Staging Area is where the Offensive musters newcomers before sending them into the fight. Exarch Larethor, a draenei, commands here beside Captain Theris Dawnhearth, a blood elf who directs the effort to win back Sun's Reach. Drill Sergeant Bahduum greets each new draft with blunt speeches: draenei who once stood with him at Skettis and in Shadowmoon Valley hear that the situation on Azeroth looks grim, and sin'dorei used to Scryer ways are told to pull their weight or get back on the boat. Vindicator Xayann fits the island's malfunctioning sentries with new crystal cores to turn them into allies, and the quartermaster Eldara Dawnrunner keeps powerful gear for those who have proven themselves.

title: Sun's Reach Sanctum
body: The Sun's Reach Sanctum is the Offensive's first goal in the town, and the key to the rest: once it is secure, its energy is to open a portal from Shattrath. The Wretched have overrun it, slipping in after they stole the power sources from its protective crystal wards. Winning it back means hunting the Wretched for the mana remnants they carry and feeding them to the wards, while Vindicator Xayann's new crystal cores turn the island's malfunctioning sentries into allies for the assault.

parts.body: The sanctum has been won, and the Offensive has made it the base for its next move. From its halls Battlemage Arynna and Harbinger Inuuro planned the fight against the Legion in the armory, and Astromancer Darnarian took up his post beside them.

title: Sun's Reach Armory
body: The Sun's Reach Armory is of great tactical importance to the Offensive, and the Burning Legion holds it. Its demons rally around the emissaries of hate, Legion shocktroopers sent to reinforce key positions, whom they fear more than any foe, and while that fear keeps their morale high the building cannot be taken. To the south the Legion's forces are tied down for now by the Scourge on the Dead Scar, but the Offensive knows that respite will not last.

parts.body: With the sanctum secure, Harbinger Inuuro sends fighters to break the demons' nerve: they slay the emissaries of hate and impale them on Shattered Sun banners for the Legion to see. Meanwhile Battlemage Arynna's dragonhawk raids on the Dead Scar keep the Legion's southern forces too busy to come to the armory's aid.

title: Sun's Reach Harbor
body: Sun's Reach Harbor is the last stronghold the Offensive needs to make the town its own, and it is held by the Dawnblade, among the most elite of Kael'thas's armies, who hold Dawnstar Village to the west as well. A ship, Silvermoon's Pride, lies at its docks. On the western docks Ayren Cloudbreaker keeps the Offensive's dragonhawks, and from the waterfront Archmage Ne'thul keeps his watch on the Sunwell Plateau.

parts.body: The harbor has fallen and the Dawnblade have been driven out. Silvermoon's Pride was taken as a prize, though she is not yet seaworthy, and Captain Valindria keeps her post aboard while she harries the naga of Greengill Coast. In the inn the alchemist Mar'nah sets up shop, though there is little she can offer until her supplies are stocked.

title: The Dawnblade Fleet
body: Off the coast of Sun's Reach ride three Dawnblade warships, the Dawnchaser, the Sin'loren and the Bloodoath, their decks crowded with reservists bound for the harbor. For all their soldiers, the ships are open to attack from the air: a rider who flies low enough can set their sails ablaze with flaming oil, then drop onto the decks while the crews struggle with the fire and can mount little defense.

parts.body: Vindicator Kaalan means to keep the fleet from reinforcing Kael's forces at the harbor before the Offensive can take it. He sends riders on Ayren Cloudbreaker's dragonhawks to burn the sails and finish the reservists on deck, reckoning that every burned sail means a long wait before the harbor sees reinforcements.

parts.body: Even with the harbor lost to them, the Dawnblade have not given it up. The fleet comes again, this time to take the harbor back, and Kaalan answers it the same way, with flaming oil from the air and blades on the burning decks.

title: Dawnstar Village
body: Dawnstar Village lies west of the Sun's Reach Armory, a blood elf village that became the stronghold of the Dawnblade on Quel'Danas. Their summoners, blood knights and marksmen fill its lanes, practicing at archery targets and training dummies, their chargers are kept close by, and Wretched prowl the outskirts. At the village's edge stands the Bloodcrystal, one of the points on the island's ley lines.

parts.body: Once the Dawnblade were driven from the harbor, their survivors fell back here. Magister Ilastar is not content to let them go: he wants every last one slain, for in his eyes they sealed their fate when they followed Kael'thas to the isle.

title: The Dawning Square
body: South of the Sun's Reach Sanctum, the Dawning Square belongs to the Burning Legion. A fel portal stands in the middle of the square, and demons guard it in force: irespeakers, unleashed hellions and abyssal flamewalkers, rallied by emissaries of hate whom they fear more than any foe. A magistrix the Offensive sent to investigate the portal never returned. The portal is also one of the points on the island's ley lines.

parts.body: Since the Sun's Reach Armory fell, this is where the Legion has fallen back, and here the Offensive keeps up the pressure, set on defeating and demoralizing the demons until their hold on the square breaks.

title: Greengill Coast
body: Greengill Coast, on the eastern shore southeast of Sun's Reach, was home to a village of Greengill murlocs until the Darkspine naga came. Their sirens now bind the murlocs with controlling orbs and set them to digging iron ore, which the naga lock in chests for shipment to the Legion. On a ley line near the shore, they have raised a shrine to Queen Azshara.

parts.body: Smith Hauthaa wants that ore for her anvil. Raiding the naga's chests arms the Offensive and robs the Legion in the same stroke, so her fighters relieve the Darkspine of their iron as often as they can.

title: The Dead Scar of Quel'Danas
body: The Dead Scar does not end at Silvermoon. On the isle it climbs from the southern shore toward the Sunwell Plateau, and its blight still stirs the dead: skeletal ravagers and frenzied ghouls wander it in great numbers. The Burning Legion has claimed the same ground, with wrath enforcers, eredar sorcerers and pit overlords, and the two hosts are locked in a struggle that keeps the demons too busy to fall upon the Offensive, at least for now.

title: Exarch Larethor
body: Exarch Larethor, a draenei, commands the Shattered Sun Staging Area. Every soldier Shattrath can spare reports to him, Aldor sent by Adyen the Lightwarden and Scryers sent by Dathris Sunstriker, and he greets them all with the same plain warning: whatever the old feud between the two orders, neither has the strength to go it alone, so they will work together, though he has a habit of calling the Scryers cryers. He has a worry of his own besides. Tyrith, a blood elf spy he embedded in the Magisters' Terrace up the rise to the east, has stopped reporting, and the exarch wants him found.

parts.body: Help reached Tyrith too late to save him, but not too late to make his death count. When the exarch heard all that had been done in the terrace, he mourned a good man and admitted he had underestimated the one who came back to tell him.

title: Captain Theris Dawnhearth
body: Captain Theris Dawnhearth, a blood elf of the Shattered Sun Offensive, directs the campaign to retake Sun's Reach from the staging area. He begins with the sanctum, sending fighters after the Wretched to recover the mana remnants they stole from its crystal wards, so that no Wretched stand in the way when the Offensive unleashes its full attack on the Legion and Kael. When Magistrix Seyla vanished while investigating the fel portal at Dawning Square, he sent help after her with a scroll taken from an enemy corpse.

parts.body: With the crystal wards around the sanctum burning again, Theris does not mean to stop there. He wants wards raised around every other building in Sun's Reach as well, for the Wretched are stubborn and go on stealing power from the crystals, and in his eyes the safety of the whole operation depends on keeping them armed.

title: Archmage Ne'thul
body: Archmage Ne'thul, a blood elf of the Shattered Sun Offensive, keeps his post aboard a boat on the waterfront at Sun's Reach Harbor, looking out toward the Sunwell Plateau to the south. While the rest of the Offensive fights for the town, his charge is the plateau itself and the Sunwell upon it, the heart of everything the enemy came to this island for. Champions sent from Shattrath to join that fight are told to seek him out when they reach the isle.

parts.body: Three mighty gates, Agamath, Rohendor and Archonisus, bar the way to the Sunwell's inner chambers, and the Shattered Sun's mages work to bring them down one by one. Ne'thul warns all who will listen that if Kil'jaeden rises through the Sunwell, the world will be thrown into a war the like of which it has not seen for ten thousand years.

parts.body: The news he gives is grim. Despite every effort, Kael'thas's sinister plans were carried out: the Sunwell was reignited in readiness for the Deceiver's arrival, and mighty barriers were raised to hold the Offensive back from its inner chambers while Kil'jaeden bore down upon the world with the full force of the Burning Legion.

title: Thalorien Dawnseeker
body: Thalorien Dawnseeker was a high elf warrior and the bearer of Quel'Delar, a sword given to his people long ago, which he carried against the Amani in the Troll Wars. When the Scourge came for the Sunwell, he stood among its defenders, and he fell on the Isle of Quel'Danas, on the ground now called the Dead Scar, buying time for his soldiers to make their own preparations. His remains still lie near the Scar's southern end, known to those who find them as those of the last wielder of Quel'Delar.

parts.body: His spirit lingers there. Called up by one who bears Quel'Delar, it relives his last stand: Thalorien orders his soldiers back to the Sunwell to prepare its defenses, swears that none of the Scourge will reach the well while he stands, and faces wave after wave of the dead with the death knight Morlen Coldgrip at their head. His sword was found long after in Icecrown, broken and defiled, where the Blood-Queen Lana'thel declared it could never be remade.

title: Magister Ilastar
body: Magister Ilastar plans the Offensive's war against the Dawnblade from the Sun's Reach Armory. To him the Dawnblade are Kael's lackeys and dogs, and he has promised to teach them a lesson in humility, sending fighters against their summoners, blood knights and marksmen. The harbor they hold matters above all to the Offensive's plans, and he means to take it from them, for once it falls, he says, the Offensive can deliver the killing blow to Kael's faltering armies.

parts.body: Victory did not soften him. With the Dawnblade driven out of the harbor and Sun's Reach won, he admitted he was not satisfied, and sent the hunt on to Dawnstar Village after the survivors, who sealed their fate when they followed Kael'thas to the isle. He likes to wonder aloud what the prince feels as his armies fall, despair, helplessness or fear, and hopes it is all of them.

title: Smith Hauthaa
body: Smith Hauthaa refuses to wait for supplies that may never arrive. Behind the Sun's Reach Armory she sets out to build an anvil and forge to arm and armor the Offensive, and she finds her iron among the enemy: the Darkspine naga of Greengill Coast are filling chests with ore bound for the Legion, and taking it hurts them as much as it helps her.

parts.body: With the anvil finished, the real work begins. She blends the naga ore into a special alloy with metal from corrupted armaments that fel orcs forged at the Ata'mal Terrace in Shadowmoon Valley, a place holy to the draenei. The anchorites have blessed her anvil so that it can cleanse them, and from it she keeps the Offensive's soldiers in weapons and armor.

title: Astromancer Darnarian
body: Astromancer Darnarian works the translocation magic of the Sun's Reach Sanctum and feels badly underappreciated for it. Everyone, he complains, wants instant gratification and never thinks of the effort behind even the simplest portal. His remedy is education. He hands visitors a crystal and sends them to attune it to the ley lines of Quel'Danas at three points: the Bloodcrystal near Dawnstar Village, the Legion's portal in the Dawning Square, and the naga shrine on Greengill Coast. Only after checking their readings does he trust them with a translocator, warning that if a reading is faulty there is no telling where they will end up, and the blame will be theirs.

title: Anchorite Ayuri
body: Anchorite Ayuri will not let the dead of Sun's Reach be forgotten. With the town won and final victory at hand, she gathers donations for a monument to those who gave their lives retaking it, with whatever remains promised to the widows and orphans of the fallen. Her fellow anchorite Kairthos admits the donations have fallen short of her hopes, and quietly invites the wealthiest champions to make up the difference, promising that all who fought here will know of their deeds.

parts.body: The Monument to the Fallen now stands in Sun's Reach. It is but a small consolation to the families, and Ayuri still collects for the orphans and spouses of the war's heroes, reminding visitors of the price of every war, even one that is won.

title: The Call to Quel'Danas
body: In Shattrath, the two rival orders serving the naaru received the same urgent summons. On the Aldor Rise, Adyen the Lightwarden admitted that his forces were spread thin and that a contingent had already gone to Azeroth to investigate events at the Sunwell Plateau, and he sent whomever he could spare to report to Larethor, wishing he could send more. On the Scryer's Tier, Dathris Sunstriker ordered every able hand back to Azeroth at once, to fight beside the Aldor of all people, for the situation called for the two orders to set their differences aside.

parts.body: On the isle, Drill Sergeant Bahduum laid out the stakes for the new recruits. Prince Kael'thas had overrun Quel'Danas, and on the plateau he and his demon allies were working to reignite the Sunwell and open a rift for Kil'jaeden. If he succeeded, this world would suffer far worse than Outland ever had. Many of them would not be going home, the sergeant warned, but those who kept their wits would have the better chance.

title: The Reclamation of Sun's Reach
body: The Offensive lacks the numbers to storm Sun's Reach outright, so it means to take the town one piece at a time. First comes the sanctum. Fighters hunt the Wretched for the mana remnants stolen from its crystal wards and use them to power the wards again, while Vindicator Xayann fits new cores into the island's malfunctioning sentries and turns them into guards. Once the sanctum is won, its energy is to open a portal from Shattrath, and the armory and the harbor must follow.

parts.body: The sanctum fell first, and word went back to Shattrath that the Offensive was making its move. Next came the armory, held by the Legion: emissaries of hate were slain and impaled on Shattered Sun banners to break the demons' nerve, while dragonhawk raids kept the Legion's southern forces busy on the Dead Scar.

title: Fire from the Sky
body: Sun's Reach is to be won from the air as much as on the ground. At the harbor, Ayren Cloudbreaker keeps the Offensive's dragonhawks ready for any rider with orders to fly, and he welcomes the work: in his line of duty one seldom sees much action, and serving this close to the front lines makes a nice change of pace. Whenever the commanders of Sun's Reach need a blow struck beyond the reach of their soldiers on the ground, it is to Ayren and his mounts that they send their fighters.

parts.body: When the Offensive moved on the armory, Battlemage Arynna knew the Legion would turn on them as soon as its forces to the south were free of the Scourge at the Dead Scar. Her answer was to keep it busy: riders flew over the Scar hurling arcane charges at pit overlords, eredar sorcerers and wrath enforcers.

parts.body: The armory fell in time, and the strikes over the Scar went on. Then Vindicator Kaalan found the riders a new target: a fleet of Dawnblade reservists sailing to reinforce the harbor. He sent them low over the ships with flaming oil to set the sails alight, then had them drop to the decks to finish the reservists.

title: The Missing Magistrix
body: Magistrix Seyla was sent to investigate the fel portal in the middle of the Dawning Square, and she never came back. Captain Theris Dawnhearth had a scroll, taken from an enemy corpse, that he believed would open the way, and he sent help through after her, with orders to find the magistrix and aid her in any way possible. Where the portal led, and whether Seyla still lived, no one at the staging area could say, and the demons crowding the square gave little cause for hope.

parts.body: The portal led to the gateway at the Throne of Kil'jaeden in Outland, by which Kael'thas's armies had retreated to the Sunwell. Seyla was alive and had little time for Theris's worry: there were much bigger problems there. Kael's most loyal followers had gorged on demon blood for days, gaining new powers, and Legion reinforcements for Quel'Danas still poured through the gateway. She set out to strip the felbloods of their stolen strength and to blast the gateway itself.

title: Thalorien's Blessing
body: Long after Thalorien Dawnseeker fell, his defiled sword Quel'Delar was found and reforged in Northrend by a champion working with the Silver Covenant or the Sunreavers. Warned by the spirit of Uther that the blade could not be trusted while the Lich King's evil clung to it, the bearer brought it to Quel'Danas to be cleansed in the Sunwell. Ranger-General Halduron Brightwing would not admit a stranger to his people's most sacred place, so lately reclaimed, on a tale alone, and set a test: seek the blessing of Thalorien's remains at the southern end of the Dead Scar.

parts.body: There the spirit relived his last stand, sending his soldiers back to the Sunwell and calling on the stranger to stand with him against the Scourge, wave after wave, and against the death knight Morlen Coldgrip.
